subject: EdgeStream: CloudLens processor rollforward — request for acknowledgement and evidence
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@edge-stream.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Notification: CloudLens onboarding as downstream processor (effective 2027-05-02)

Hi Naomi & Irene,

Quick heads up: EdgeStream is onboarding a downstream analytics processor, CloudLens Analytics (cloudlens@cloudlens.io). They will process anonymized telemetry and derived usage metrics from our ingestion pipeline to power session analytics and aggregated dashboards for EdgeStream customers. The effective cutover date is 2027-05-02.

Scope summary:
- Data types: telemetry, aggregated usage metrics, service-level logs (no customer-submitted documents).
- Purpose: analytics, feature usage, performance monitoring.
- Locations: primary processing in AWS us-west-2; EU processing in eu-west-1 for EU-tenants.
- Cross-border transfers: yes — derived metrics may be aggregated across regions for global dashboards.

Attached: CloudLens-SOC2-summary.pdf (summary), CloudLens-dataflow-Apr2027.png (draft dataflow), DPA-addendum-EdgeStream-Redwood.docx (proposed addendum). We uploaded the same to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XyzEdgeStreamEvidence

Request: please acknowledge receipt and let us know if Redwood requires additional evidence (encryption attestation, onshore fallback, KMS details, contractual language edits). If you'd prefer, we can set up a 30-min call with our Security Ops and CloudLens technical lead next week.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Rivera
Security & Compliance
EdgeStream Solutions
attachments: [CloudLens-SOC2-summary.pdf, CloudLens-dataflow-Apr2027.png, DPA-addendum-EdgeStream-Redwood.docx]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notification: CloudLens onboarding as downstream processor (effective 2027-05-02)

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the attachments. A few clarifying questions before we ack formally to our legal/procurement teams: 

1) Data scope: can you confirm CloudLens will not receive raw PII or full customer documents? The note above says "no customer-submitted documents" but we'd like explicit confirmation.
2) Retention: what retention windows will CloudLens apply to raw logs and aggregated/derived metrics?
3) Encryption & keys: is data at rest encrypted with customer-segregated KMS keys or a shared AWS-managed key? If you use AWS KMS, please attach the key policy or an attestation.
4) Onshore fallback: for regulated EU customers, is there a static onshore fallback option (i.e., forced processing in eu-west-1 only) or any tenant-residency controls?
5) Evidence: the SOC2 summary is helpful — do you have a mapping (CSV or doc) tying controls to our DPA clauses (encryption, access controls, subprocessors)?

Please upload any additional evidence to the Drive folder and paste links here. Also flag whether you need Redwood to sign the DPA addendum as-is or if you anticipate counsels exchanging edits.

We try to close these within the two-week window prior to cutover; if you can provide answers by EOD 2027-04-25 we can proceed with an internal acknowledgement.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Privacy Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rivera <alex@edge-stream.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notification: CloudLens onboarding as downstream processor (effective 2027-05-02)

Hi Naomi / Marissa / Irene — apologies for the delay; we waited to finalize CloudLens' encryption attestation and retention policy. Answers below and artifacts are uploaded to the Drive link from my earlier note. DocuSign link for the DPA addendum is here: https://www.docusign.com/edge-dpa-addendum/ABCDEFG

Short answers to Naomi's questions:
- Raw PII/documents: confirmed — CloudLens will not receive raw customer documents or any customer-submitted files. They receive structured telemetry and derived aggregates only.
- Retention: raw logs (30 days), derived aggregates (90 days), dashboards (rolling 13 months). We included retention policy in the CloudLens-dataflow-Apr2027.png and the SOC2 summary.
- Encryption & keys: data at rest is encrypted using AWS KMS. For EU-tenants we will use a customer-segregated KMS alias (kms:arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111222333:key/eu-specific-key). Key policy excerpt attached as CloudLens-KMS-policy.txt in the Drive.
- Onshore fallback: yes — for EU-tenant tagging we can route processing to eu-west-1 only (tenant residency control). It is implemented as a processing flag in the ingestion pipeline and will be available at cutover.
- Controls mapping: we prepared a concise controls mapping CSV (CloudLens-controls-mapping.csv) that shows SOC2 controls -> DPA clauses. It's in the Drive.

Attachments uploaded: CloudLens-SOC2-summary.pdf, CloudLens-dataflow-Apr2027.png, CloudLens-KMS-policy.txt, CloudLens-controls-mapping.csv. Procurement questionnaire (completed) uploaded to HS ticket HS-58291.

If you need anything else prior to 2027-05-02, please let me know — happy to join the scheduled call.

Best,
Alex Rivera
Security & Compliance
EdgeStream Solutions
